newsitem.title: USA: Fla. judge allows tobacco to pursue prison claims.
newsitem.headline: Fla. judge allows tobacco to pursue prison claims.

text.p: A Florida judge ruled Monday that tobacco companies may introduce evidence showing that the state of Florida was partly responsible for smoking-related injuries sustained by Medicaid patients because it once made and sold cigarettes.

Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen handed down the ruling during the first of what are expected to be eight days of pre-trial hearings designed to eliminate extraneous issues before the state's Medicaid lawsuit against the tobacco industry goes to trial on August 4.

In making the ruling, Cohen said he would allow the tobacco companies to introduce that evidence in the case because it relates "to market share and the dividing up of the state responsibility for share (of health-related costs)."

During the pre-trial hearing, the tobacco companies introduced evidence that the state of Florida had been manufacturing and selling cigarettes since 1935 and that at its peak production year, 1978, it sold 6.1 million packages of cigarettes in prisons, schools and hospitals across the state.
Florida was one of 40 states to file suit against big tobacco seeking to recoup public health costs of treating people with smoking-related illnesses.
